quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Weave between lane positions to keep other drivers away.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Protect you the same as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A face shield is better because it protects your whole face. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a break every two hours to avoid getting too tired.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. Follow all the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When riding, space around your motorcycle helps you to:
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to move safely.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the bump better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: The best gear to wear while riding is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you. Use a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: You can be more visible by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to ride on empty roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if necessary. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates on roads are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car. Always do a thorough check of your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol and wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have impaired abilities.
You will be safe if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have impaired abilities.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your body. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always look over your shoulder to check for vehicles or hazards before changing lanes.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a motorcycle group small is:

options.text: A small group is less likely to separate in traffic.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up.
It will be hard to track everyone's location.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less likely to separate in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups are better than large groups. They are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to separate at traffic lights, and do not pressure slower riders to speed up.
